## 6. System architecture

One React SPA, one mobile app, one NestJS modular monolith deployed as two processes (API and worker), one PostgreSQL cluster, Redis for cache and queues, and S3 for files — all in AWS Mumbai. Modules are separated by code boundaries and table ownership, so any one can be extracted into a service later without a data rewrite.

![high-level architecture · clients, edge, monolith, data, third parties](data:image/png;base64,)

high-level architecture · clients, edge, monolith, data, third parties

Read top to bottom: every client enters through the same edge and API; the worker does all slow or external work, so a provider outage never blocks a punch or an approval. A warm standby in ap-south-2 (Hyderabad) holds replicated snapshots and files.

### 6.1 Request pipeline (every protected call)

1. Edge: CloudFront + AWS WAF (OWASP rules, geo/IP rate limits) → ALB.
2. Authenticate: session cookie (web) or bearer token (mobile/API key).
3. Resolve tenant context: user → active membership → tenant status (active) → subscription entitlements. Never from the body or a stale session column.
4. Authorise: permission key + scope resolver + field classification (Section 8.1).
5. Validate DTO (class-validator/Zod); reject unknown fields.
6. Handler/service: Prisma queries always filtered by tenant_id; Postgres session variable app.tenant_id set per transaction for RLS defence in depth.
7. Same transaction: domain write + audit_events + outbox_events.
8. Response envelope with correlationId.

### 6.2 Frontend architecture

| Concern      | Choice                                                                        |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Framework    | React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Vite (CF-40)                                 |
| UI kit       | Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (Radix primitives), lucide icons                     |
| Server state | TanStack Query (query keys include tenant ID; cache cleared on tenant switch) |
| Client state | Zustand (UI prefs, tenant switcher, wizard drafts) — no Redux                 |
| Forms        | React Hook Form + Zod (schemas shared via packages/contracts)                 |
| Routing      | React Router 6 with lazy-loaded module routes and route guards (UX only)      |
| Tables       | TanStack Table with server-side pagination/sort/filter                        |
| Charts       | Recharts                                                                      |
| API client   | Generated from OpenAPI (openapi-typescript + fetch wrapper with CSRF header)  |
| i18n         | i18next, strings externalised from day one                                    |
| Testing      | Jest + React Testing Library; Playwright E2E; axe-core a11y                   |
| Hosting      | S3 + CloudFront (or Vercel), immutable hashed assets                          |

### 6.4 Asynchronous work (worker process)

| Queue            | Jobs                                                                             |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| outbox           | Relay outbox events to channel queues and webhooks                               |
| email, sms, push | Provider delivery with retry/backoff                                             |
| files            | Malware scan (ClamAV container), thumbnail, PDF generation (letters, payslips)   |
| attendance       | Device sync, nightly day finaliser, absent marking, auto-checkout                |
| leave            | Accrual (monthly), year-end, comp-off expiry                                     |
| payroll          | Calculation per employee chunk (100/job), payslip generation, statutory files    |
| reports          | Exports, scheduled reports                                                       |
| imports          | Parse, validate, commit                                                          |
| lifecycle        | Future-dated assignment changes, probation reminders, exit-day access revocation |
| housekeeping     | Expired sessions/tokens, abandoned uploads, retention purge, partition creation  |

All scheduled jobs are idempotent per (tenant, job, period) and carry validated tenant context.

## 7. Database architecture

PostgreSQL 16 (Amazon RDS, Multi-AZ) is the only system of record: shared database, shared schema, tenant_id on every tenant-owned row, composite tenant-safe foreign keys, and Row-Level Security as a second line of defence. The full data dictionary (every table with purpose, PK, FKs, relationships, classification and retention) is workbook tab DB-Tables; DB build tasks are tab S06.

### 7.1 Conventions

| Rule               | Standard                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary keys       | id uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() (UUID v7 generated in app for index locality is acceptable)                                                                          |
| Tenancy            | tenant_id uuid NOT NULL on tenant-owned tables; every parent has UNIQUE (tenant_id, id); every child FK is (tenant_id, parent_id) → parent(tenant_id, id)              |
| Legal-entity scope | legal_entity_id where the record belongs to an employer; FK (tenant_id, legal_entity_id)                                                                               |
| Time               | timestamptz UTC for instants; date for business dates; IANA timezone stored where calculations need it                                                                 |
| Effective dating   | Half-open \[effective_from, effective_to); effective_to NULL = current; overlap prevented by EXCLUDE USING gist with btree_gist                                        |
| Money              | NUMERIC(18,2) + currency char(3); rates NUMERIC(18,6)                                                                                                                  |
| Enums              | text + CHECK for fixed system states; lookup tables for tenant-configurable values                                                                                     |
| Audit columns      | created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, version int (optimistic locking)                                                                                       |
| Soft delete        | deleted_at only on masters and documents; never on ledgers, payroll, audit, outbox                                                                                     |
| JSONB              | Extensible metadata, policy documents (with JSON-Schema version), event payloads — never for columns used in joins, authorization or money                             |
| Encryption         | Restricted columns stored as bytea ciphertext + \*\_last4 / \*\_hash for search                                                                                        |
| Indexes            | Lead with tenant_id; partial indexes for status = 'pending'; FK columns indexed                                                                                        |
| Partitioning       | Monthly range partitions for punches, audit_events, outbox_events, notification_deliveries; pg_partman                                                                 |
| RLS                | Enabled on tenant tables with policy tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid; app sets it with SET LOCAL per transaction; platform jobs use a separate role |
| Migrations         | Prisma Migrate + raw SQL files for composite FKs, exclusion constraints, RLS, partitions                                                                               |

## 8. Security architecture

Security is deny-by-default and enforced only on the server: every request is checked for identity, active membership, tenant status, permission, scope, field class and record state before any row is read. The single highest risk is cross-tenant exposure, so isolation is enforced three times — in the service layer, by composite foreign keys, and by Postgres RLS.

### 8.1 Authorization: RBAC + ABAC

**RBAC.** Permission keys follow module.resource.action (e.g. leave.request.approve, employee.restricted.read, payroll.run.approve). The global catalog starts with 238 feature-level keys (workbook S09 lists them per feature). Roles bundle keys; grants bind a role to a membership with a scope and optional validity window.

**ABAC.** After RBAC passes, attribute rules apply:

| Attribute    | Rule example                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scope        | Target employee must fall in the grant's scope (SELF, TEAM, TEAM_TREE, DEPARTMENT, LOCATION, LEGAL_ENTITY, ORGANIZATION, ASSIGNED)                                                      |
| Field class  | Public / Internal / Sensitive PII / Restricted: response serialiser strips fields above the caller's clearance; restricted reveal needs \*.restricted.read and logs to data_access_logs |
| Record state | Locked payroll run, closed cycle, locked attendance period → no mutation                                                                                                                |
| Relationship | Requester ≠ approver; maker ≠ checker; interviewer assigned to interview                                                                                                                |
| Time         | Grant validity window; break-glass expiry                                                                                                                                               |
| Tenant state | active only; suspended read-blocked; entitlement must include the module                                                                                                                |
| Context      | MFA verified in this session for restricted actions (step-up within 15 min)                                                                                                             |

Implementation: one PolicyEngine in common/authz used by guards (route level) and by repositories (row filter builder producing the scope WHERE clause). Lists and exports call the same builder, so they cannot drift.

### 8.2 Authentication, MFA and SSO

| Control                   | Standard                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Password hashing          | Argon2id (m = 19 MiB, t = 2, p = 1 minimum; tune to ~250 ms)                                                                                                                                               |
| Password policy           | Min 12 chars, no composition rules, blocked if in breached corpus (HIBP k-anonymity), no reuse of last 5, no forced periodic expiry (NIST 800-63B)                                                         |
| Lockout                   | 5 failures / 15 min per account + IP throttling; CAPTCHA after 3                                                                                                                                           |
| Sessions (web)            | HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies; access 15 min; refresh 30 d sliding, rotate each use, family revoke on reuse; idle timeout 30 min (tenant-configurable 15–120); absolute 12 h for privileged roles |
| CSRF                      | Double-submit token header X-CSRF-Token on all non-GET                                                                                                                                                     |
| Mobile / API              | OAuth 2.0 + PKCE; bearer access 15 min; rotating refresh in secure storage; API keys hashed, scoped, expiring                                                                                              |
| MFA                       | TOTP (RFC 6238) + 10 recovery codes; WebAuthn/passkeys in Phase 8; mandatory for SA, PSUP, OA, HR, PAY, FIN                                                                                                |
| SSO                       | SAML 2.0 and OIDC per tenant (Phase 8); enforce-SSO toggle; password login disabled for SSO users except break-glass owner account                                                                         |
| Provisioning              | SCIM 2.0 users/groups (Phase 8)                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Device/session visibility | Users see and revoke active sessions; new-device login email                                                                                                                                               |

### 8.3 Audit trail

Every sensitive mutation, approval decision, role change, login event, restricted read, export, policy activation, break-glass action and integration change writes audit_events inside the business transaction. Records are immutable (INSERT-only DB grant), carry request_id, session_id, source, reason, and are searchable by OA/AUD/CMP within their scope.

### 8.4 Encryption and key management

| Layer       | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| In transit  | TLS 1.2+ everywhere, including RDS and Redis (in-transit encryption on)                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| At rest     | RDS, EBS, S3, ElastiCache encrypted with AWS KMS CMKs per environment                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Field level | Restricted fields (bank account, PAN, Aadhaar reference, UAN, salary amounts in exports, tax IDs of entities) encrypted with AES-256-GCM using per-tenant data keys wrapped by KMS (envelope encryption); keys rotated yearly; blind index (HMAC) for exact-match search |
| Files       | S3 SSE-KMS; bucket public access blocked; Object Ownership enforced; presigned URLs ≤ 5 min                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Secrets     | AWS Secrets Manager; rotated; never in env files committed to Git                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Backups     | Encrypted snapshots; cross-region copy (Hyderabad ap-south-2) encrypted with a separate key                                                                                                                                                                              |

### 8.5 Privacy: DPDP Act 2023 and GDPR considerations

The tenant is the Data Fiduciary for its employees; we are the Data Processor. Controls built to support both:

- **Data inventory** per field: purpose, class, legal basis (employment/legitimate use vs. consent), retention, access roles (tab DB-Tables).
- **Notice and consent:** candidate consent at application; employee privacy notice acknowledgement at first login; consent records versioned.
- **Data-principal rights:** access (self-export of own data), correction (profile change requests), erasure (anonymise where statutory retention forbids deletion), grievance with due dates.
- **Minimisation:** Aadhaar not stored in full by default; government IDs collected only when a document type with a stated purpose requires them.
- **Breach response:** runbook with 72-hour clock to notify the tenant (who notifies the Data Protection Board/individuals as their counsel decides).
- **Cross-border:** all primary data in India; sub-processors listed (email, SMS, error tracking) with data-processing terms; Sentry and logs scrub PII.
- **GDPR readiness** for future EU tenants: same controls plus SCCs and EU region option; not claimed until reviewed (DEC-015).

### 8.6 Data retention (defaults pending legal sign-off)

| Data class                      | Default retention after trigger                  | Trigger               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| Payroll, statutory, tax records | 8 years                                          | End of financial year |
| Employee master and documents   | 8 years (configurable)                           | Exit date             |
| Candidate data (not hired)      | 12 months                                        | Last activity         |
| Attendance punches and selfies  | Punches 8 years; selfies 90 days                 | Capture               |
| Security/auth audit             | 2 years                                          | Event                 |
| Business mutation audit         | 8 years for payroll-linked, 1 year others        | Event                 |
| Operational logs                | 90 days                                          | Event                 |
| Exports                         | 24 h link; file purged at 7 days                 | Creation              |
| Tenant data after cancellation  | 90 days, then purge (backups age out in 35 days) | Cancellation          |

Legal hold suspends purge for the held scope until released (both actions audited).

### 8.7 Application security controls

- OWASP ASVS L2 checklist; security headers (CSP with nonces, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy).
- Input validation at DTO boundary; parameterised queries only (Prisma; raw SQL via tagged templates).
- Rate limits: auth 10/min/IP, general 600/min/user, export 10/hour/user; 429 with Retry-After.
- File uploads: type allowlist, magic-byte sniffing, size caps, ClamAV scan, quarantine bucket prefix, no inline rendering of HTML/SVG.
- SSRF guard on webhooks and URL fetches; outbound egress via NAT with allowlist.
- Dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk), SAST (Semgrep/CodeQL), container scan (Trivy), secret scanning (Gitleaks) on every PR.
- Annual third-party penetration test; first before the first enterprise go-live.
- Logs never contain passwords, tokens, full bank/PAN/Aadhaar values, payslip contents.

### 8.8 Threats and controls (summary)

| Threat                        | Primary control                                                                                                                               | Verified by                       |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Cross-tenant IDOR             | Server tenant context + composite FKs + RLS + 404 masking                                                                                     | SEC-TEN-001/002 on every endpoint |
| Privilege escalation          | Grant ceiling, no self-grant, platform roles unassignable                                                                                     | SEC-RBAC-001                      |
| Session theft/replay          | HttpOnly cookies, rotation, family revoke, step-up MFA                                                                                        | AUTH-002                          |
| Malicious upload              | Scan before availability                                                                                                                      | FILE-001                          |
| Payroll fraud (bank change)   | Bank change approval + MFA step-up + notification to employee + cooling period (no payout to new account within 48 h of change, configurable) | PAY tests                         |
| Insider over-access           | Field classes, restricted-read logging, monthly access review report                                                                          | Audit review                      |
| Export leakage                | Separate export permission, scope reuse, expiring links, formula neutralisation                                                               | RPT-001                           |
| Workflow race / self-approval | Optimistic locking, requester ≠ approver                                                                                                      | WF-001                            |
| Import poisoning              | Preview/commit, idempotency, formula neutralisation                                                                                           | IMP-001/002/003                   |

## 9. Scalability, deployment and operations

The design load (500 tenants, 100,000 employees, 5,000 concurrent users) fits a modest footprint: 2–6 API containers, 2–4 workers, one Multi-AZ Postgres with a read replica, and one Redis cluster. Scaling beyond that is horizontal for compute and read replicas plus partitioning for data, before any service split.

### 9.1 Scalability design

| Concern               | Design                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Multi-tenant strategy | Shared DB/shared schema (pool model) for all tenants. Large tenants (> 10,000 employees) can move to a dedicated Postgres cluster (silo) behind the same code via a tenant → connection routing map; no schema change                    |
| Noisy neighbour       | Per-tenant API rate limits; per-tenant queue concurrency caps (e.g. payroll 4 parallel jobs/tenant); report jobs queued with fairness                                                                                                    |
| Caching               | Redis: permission sets per membership (TTL 5 min, busted on grant change), tenant settings and entitlements (TTL 10 min, busted on change), holiday calendars, dashboard aggregates (TTL 60 s). Cache keys always prefixed t:{tenantId}: |
| HTTP caching          | CDN for static assets (immutable, 1 year); API responses no-store except public careers page (60 s)                                                                                                                                      |
| Queues                | BullMQ on Redis with named queues (6.4), dead-letter queues, rate-limited processors; the outbox table remains the durable source                                                                                                        |
| Background jobs       | Idempotent per (tenant, job, period); chunked (100 employees per payroll job); resumable                                                                                                                                                 |
| Horizontal scaling    | Stateless API on ECS Fargate behind ALB; auto-scale on CPU 60% and p95 latency; workers auto-scale on queue depth                                                                                                                        |
| Database scaling      | RDS Postgres (start db.r6g.large, Multi-AZ); PgBouncer/RDS Proxy for connection pooling; read replica for reports/exports; monthly partitions for high-volume tables; archive cold partitions to S3 (Parquet) for analytics              |
| Load balancing        | ALB with health checks (/health/live, /health/ready), slow-start, cross-zone                                                                                                                                                             |
| CDN                   | CloudFront for web app, careers pages and public assets; signed URLs never cached                                                                                                                                                        |
| Search                | Postgres full-text + pg_trgm for directory and candidates; OpenSearch only if p95 search > 500 ms at scale                                                                                                                               |
| Analytics (Phase 8)   | Nightly CDC to a warehouse schema (or Redshift Serverless) for custom reports; never query OLTP for heavy analytics                                                                                                                      |

### 9.2 Deployment environments

| Environment   | Purpose                                                                                                        | Data                                   | Access                               |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Local         | Developer machines via Docker Compose (Postgres, Redis, MinIO, MailHog, ClamAV)                                | Synthetic seed                         | Developers                           |
| CI            | Ephemeral per PR: migrations from empty DB, unit/integration/contract/isolation tests                          | Synthetic                              | Pipeline only                        |
| Dev           | Shared integration of main; auto-deploy                                                                        | Synthetic                              | Engineering                          |
| Testing (QA)  | Release candidates; full regression, security scans, performance smoke                                         | Synthetic + anonymised fixtures        | QA, engineering                      |
| UAT / Staging | Production-like (same Terraform, smaller sizes); customer acceptance, migration rehearsal, restore drills      | Masked copies or customer test tenants | QA, PO, customer pilots              |
| Production    | Live tenants, AWS ap-south-1, 3 AZs                                                                            | Real                                   | Restricted, MFA, just-in-time access |
| DR            | Warm standby in ap-south-2 (Hyderabad): cross-region snapshots + S3 replication + Terraform to rebuild compute | Replicated                             | Ops on incident                      |

**Release flow.** Trunk-based development; PR checks (lint, typecheck, unit, integration, isolation, contract, SAST, dependency, secret scan) → merge → build immutable images (SBOM) → Dev → Testing → Staging (migration rehearsal + E2E) → approval → production: run migrations with a dedicated migration role → blue/green API deploy → canary 10% for 15 min → full. Feature flags gate unfinished and policy-gated features (attendance rules, payroll native, finance, billing tax).

### 9.3 Disaster recovery and backup

| Item                 | Strategy                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database backups     | RDS automated backups with PITR (35-day retention); daily snapshot copied cross-region; monthly snapshot kept 1 year                                 |
| Object storage       | S3 versioning + 30-day noncurrent retention; cross-region replication of document buckets; Object Lock (governance) for payslips and statutory files |
| Redis                | Not a source of truth; rebuilt from DB/outbox                                                                                                        |
| Config and secrets   | Terraform state versioned; Secrets Manager replicated to DR region                                                                                   |
| RPO / RTO            | RPO ≤ 15 min (PITR), RTO ≤ 4 h (region failover playbook)                                                                                            |
| Restore drills       | Monthly restore of production snapshot into isolated account with row-count and journey checks; quarterly full DR game day                           |
| Tenant-level restore | Point-in-time restore to a side database, then targeted, audited copy-back for one tenant (runbook)                                                  |

### 9.4 Monitoring, logging and alerts

| Layer    | Tooling                                                                       | What is watched                                                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Errors   | Sentry (FE, BE, mobile) with PII scrubbing                                    | New issues, error rate per release                                                             |
| Metrics  | CloudWatch + Prometheus-compatible (Amazon Managed Prometheus) + Grafana      | RED metrics per route, DB CPU/connections/locks, queue depth/lag, job failures, cache hit rate |
| Traces   | OpenTelemetry → AWS X-Ray or Grafana Tempo                                    | Slow requests, N+1 queries                                                                     |
| Logs     | Structured JSON → CloudWatch Logs → OpenSearch (30 days hot, 90 days archive) | request_id, tenant_id, user_id (hashed), route, latency, outcome                               |
| Uptime   | External synthetic checks every 1 min from 3 locations                        | Login, punch, health                                                                           |
| Security | GuardDuty, CloudTrail, WAF logs, app security events                          | Auth anomalies, privilege changes, export spikes                                               |
| Business | Custom dashboards                                                             | Payroll run failures, outbox backlog, email bounce rate, device sync gaps                      |

**Alert policy (paging via PagerDuty/Opsgenie)**

| Alert                              | Threshold                     | Severity                       |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| API 5xx rate                       | \> 2% for 5 min               | P1 page                        |
| p95 latency                        | \> 1 s for 10 min             | P2                             |
| Cross-tenant authorization denials | \> 20/min from one membership | P1 security                    |
| Outbox pending age                 | \> 5 min                      | P2                             |
| Dead-letter jobs                   | any payroll/statutory job     | P1                             |
| DB CPU / connections               | \> 80% for 15 min             | P2                             |
| Replica lag                        | \> 60 s                       | P3                             |
| Backup failure                     | any                           | P1                             |
| Break-glass session opened         | any                           | Notify security + tenant owner |
| Certificate expiry                 | < 21 days                     | P3                             |

Every alert links a runbook (workbook RISK tab references): data exposure, credential compromise, failed migration, stuck import, duplicate payment, file quarantine spike, provider outage.

Rules the matrix cannot show, enforced by the policy engine:

- Super Admin never reads tenant HR records; only platform objects and, with break-glass, a time-boxed view.
- Approve (A) is never valid on one's own request; maker ≠ checker for payroll runs, finance journals and expense audit.
- Interviewers (not shown) see only assigned interviews; Candidates only their own portal token.
- Granting is capped at the grantor's own permissions and scope; platform roles are never assignable in a tenant.

## 11. Development execution plan

The full product is 1,567 story points across 287 features, which is 29 two-week sprints for two squads — 16 Nov 2026 to 24 Dec 2027 — with the first production release for pilot tenants after Phase 3 (mid-May 2027). Dates assume ~70 points per sprint at full velocity with a ramp-up in sprints 1–3 (A-04, A-38); change the start date and sprint length in tab S13-Sprint-Plan and every date recalculates.

Phases run back to back; the pilot release after Phase 3 is the first point a paying customer runs attendance, leave and core HR in production.

### 11.2 Sequencing notes

- Phase order follows the brief (Payroll before Recruitment). Recruitment has no dependency on payroll, so a third squad could pull Phase 5 forward to run alongside Phase 4 and finish ~6 weeks earlier.
- Phase 3 ends with the first production release. If any gate evidence is missing, insert one hardening sprint before go-live rather than carrying debt into payroll.
- Every phase starts a fresh sprint after its gate, so a slipped gate delays only the next phase.
- Gated features (attendance rules, statutory payroll, finance posting, billing tax) are built on schedule but stay off until the named owner signs.

## 12. Gap analysis

The biggest gaps in the source packs were whole modules the brief requires (travel, helpdesk, assets, LMS depth, mobile, statutory detail) and the absence of any HR policy content — attendance and leave rules, statutory rates and retention periods are still unsigned. The three highest risks are cross-tenant exposure, native payroll accuracy and scope size for a small team.

| Organization | Branches, grades, cost centers, statutory registrations                                                          | M03                |
| Attendance   | GPS geofence, selfie, IP restriction, biometric sync, kiosk, offline mobile, OT, comp-off, contractor timesheets | M10, M11           |
| Leave        | Accrual, carry-forward, encashment, sandwich rule, restricted holidays, leave on behalf, year-end                | M12                |
| Payroll      | Loans, arrears, off-cycle, bank formats, GL export, F&F detail, variance review                                  | M13                |

| Lifecycle    | Pre-joining portal, document verification, no-show, resignation, clearances, exit interview, rehire flag         | M08, M09           |

All 102 are marked **New** in the register and each is mirrored as an assumption (tab ASSUME), so the PO can strike any before Phase 1.

### 12.2 Risk register (top 12 of 28)

| ID   | Type        | Risk                                                      | Impact   | Mitigation                                                                |
| ---- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R-01 | Security    | Cross-tenant data exposure through a missed tenant filter | Critical | Composite FKs + RLS + central scope builder + isolation suite on every PR |
| R-02 | Security    | Privilege escalation via grants or custom roles           | Critical | Permission ceiling, no self-grant, negative tests                         |
| R-03 | Business    | Native payroll miscalculation → statutory penalties       | Critical | Exchange first; signed rule sets; 2-period parallel run; maker-checker    |
| R-20 | Operational | Backups exist but restore untested                        | Critical | Monthly restore drills                                                    |
| R-04 | Business    | Statutory rules change mid-year                           | High     | Effective-dated rule sets with sources; monthly rule review               |
| R-05 | Technical   | Attendance edge cases (overnight, drift) give wrong days  | High     | HR-signed golden fixtures; property-based tests                           |
| R-06 | Technical   | Leave balance races                                       | High     | Ledger + FOR UPDATE projection; concurrency tests                         |
| R-07 | Business    | Scope creep: 31 modules for a small team                  | High     | Phase gates; P0 first; change control                                     |
| R-16 | Security    | Payroll fraud via bank detail change                      | High     | Approval + MFA step-up + notification + 48 h cooling                      |
| R-12 | Privacy     | DPDP non-compliance                                       | High     | M23 controls; legal review before GA                                      |
| R-13 | Business    | Data-residency demands                                    | High     | AWS Mumbai + Hyderabad DR                                                 |
| R-24 | Operational | Key-person dependency                                     | High     | ADRs, runbooks, pairing, this SSOT                                        |

Grouped by type: technical risks R-05, R-06, R-09, R-14, R-18, R-23, R-27; business risks R-03, R-04, R-07, R-08, R-13, R-17, R-21, R-26; security risks R-01, R-02, R-11, R-16, R-19, R-25; privacy/compliance R-12, R-22, R-28; operational R-10, R-15, R-20, R-24. Full register with likelihood and owners: tab RISK.
